title: Noninteractive CLI failure exit status
objective: Make uncaught compile and runtime failures from piped or redirected Sage.js CLI input exit nonzero without changing interactive REPL behavior or broken-pipe handling

oracles: Node subprocess exit-status assertions in Python and Sage modes

handoff.summary: Noninteractive REPL input now latches exit status 1 whenever an uncaught user compile, lowering, load, timing, runtime, or result-print failure is reported. TTY input retains the interactive contract of reporting errors and continuing without changing the process status. Focused CLI coverage includes successful Python input; Python and Sage runtime failures; syntax failures; an async-function failure; an EOF-flushed compound suite; a synthetic TTY session; and an early-closing stdout consumer.
risks: Broad integration receipts are intentionally deferred: parallel native-cache preparation downgraded this fresh worktree's self-hosted compiler to the checked-in bootstrap artifact. The compiler was manually reconverged and the focused CLI suite passes; a separate integration lane is fixing that cache/bootstrap defect.
next_steps: After the cache/bootstrap fix lands, merge or rebase that foundation, run the integration lane's architecture, portable, strict-baselib, and CLI validations, and set this contract to review.
